title: Intel beat on earnings, so why is the stock sinking?
summary: Intel topped quarterly earnings estimates, but its fourth-quarter revenue outlook came in roughly $1.5 billion below what investors hoped for, sending the shares sharply lower in after-hours trading. On Yahoo Finance's Market Domination Overtime, Patrick Moorhead of Moor Insights & Strategy explains that a shortage of memory chips and soaring memory prices have shrunk the PC market, though he argues buyers are only delaying purchases rather than disappearing. He also sees a big opportunity in AI data centers, where generative and agentic AI need many more CPUs alongside accelerators, and discusses Intel's foundry ambitions and what management must say to reassure investors.
focus: Shadow the analyst's answer on memory prices and the PC slump, where he explains why delayed demand will eventually return, and his short explanation of why AI servers need roughly one CPU per accelerator; both are fast, conversational passages packed with industry vocabulary.
